profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap node in Riverside County, California, is tagged telecom=data_center under the name "IT," a bare two-letter label that reads as an abbreviation for information technology rather than a distinctive company or product name. Genuine data center operators in California nearly always brand their facilities with a company name, colocation product line, or campus identifier, so a label this generic is much more consistent with a placeholder tag, a mapping shorthand for an IT closet or server room inside a larger building, or an incomplete edit than with a standalone, named commercial data center. Public location records place the coordinates tied to this entry near Riverwalk Parkway, an office and light industrial corridor in Riverside County with a mix of business park tenants, and no business at that address carries the name "IT" or anything resembling it in available public directories. No operator website, business registration, trade press coverage, or permit record could be tied to this tag. Given the combination of a non distinctive name and the absence of any corroborating public record, this entry is best read as an unresolved or likely mistagged point in OpenStreetMap rather than a documented data center. Readers should treat the data center classification here as unconfirmed until a public identity for the underlying business, if any exists, surfaces.

reading.body:
A data center tag in Riverside County, California cannot be tied to any operator, and should be treated as unconfirmed rather than counted as AI capacity.

The entry is an OpenStreetMap node named only "IT," tagged telecom=data_center. That two-letter label reads as an abbreviation for information technology, not as a company or campus name. Reverse geocoding of the stored coordinates resolves to Riverwalk Parkway, an office and light industrial corridor. No operator website, business registration, permit record, or trade press coverage matches the tag or the address.

The absence of a name is the substantive finding. Data center operators brand facilities with company names, colocation product lines, or campus identifiers, so a generic label is more consistent with a placeholder, an IT closet or server room inside a larger building, or an incomplete edit. Power capacity, rack count, cooling, certifications, and commissioning status are all unpublished, so the site cannot be assessed for AI infrastructure relevance at all.

California carries 103 mapped data center points, of which 11 publish power specifications totaling 365 MW. This entry would rank twelfth by published capacity if its specifications were known, but that ranking means nothing while the facility itself is unconfirmed. The data covers one unresolved map point and the state's published-specification count. It does not establish that a data center exists at these coordinates, and it says nothing about the grid, power, or buildings beyond the fact that most mapped California points, like this one, publish no capacity figure.
